name: record-scaffolding-merge-limits
body: Five limits. (1) The merged files map is unioned and never pruned against the manifest, so a path deleted in an earlier scan can keep a later-retired module alive until a full-scan extraction replaces the record. (2) A pure-intermediate module with no files entry whose only parent module is retired survives as an orphan module with no parent edge until a full scan re-extracts; upgrade if the retirement walk must cascade through the stored Module-to-Module tree or prune stale file paths. (3) `record` reads the delta baseline `State` through a separate store open before it opens its write transaction, because loading while the write transaction holds `facts.lock` would self-contend for the bounded budget; upgrade to a `FactStore`-taking `State::load_from` if the store ever forbids same-process double-open. (4) The collector now runs twice per successful scan — here at the record boundary (authoritative) and again in `cmd_scan` after `run_pipeline` returns; the second pass finds nothing to collect and is a no-op read, so it is harmless, but the `src/scan.rs` duplicate could be deleted later once nothing needs it (task 4's file, outside this task's single-file scope). (5) A contended intent clear can add up to the ~30 s writer-wait budget after an otherwise successful record commit, because the clear re-acquires `facts.lock`; it is best-effort so it never fails the scan, but if that latency matters the clear should be made non-blocking rather than fatal.
